title: Introduce tenant zone-locker middleware, operator KMS lease shim, and audit-stripper profiles
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers in regulated regions require per-tenant enforcement that incoming requests are pinned to an allowed geo zone and that any KMS operations use an ephemeral operator lease tied to the asserted zone. This PR implements a lightweight "zone-locker" middleware to normalize/respect tenant zone assertions, an operator KMS lease shim to create short-lived operator-scoped credentials for cross-tenant KMS orchestration, and an "audit-stripper" profile that redacts sensitive context from high-volume logs while preserving compliance anchors. Motivation: reduce blast radius for cross-region operator actions, make KMS usage auditable and proofable, and lower PII exposure in high-cardinality audit streams. Changes include: 1) request-time zone assertor that enforces tenant zone from token/headers with configurable soft/hard modes; 2) operator KMS lease flow that leverages existing CMK allocator but issues ephemeral operator leases with signed residency assertions; 3) pluggable audit-stripper pipeline stage with configurable redaction profiles per-route. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked: internal/doc/tenant-zone-locker.md - [x] unit & integration tests added - [x] staged rollout flags (feature gate) - [x] documented runtime knobs in CLI and Helm - [x] linear tasks closed: ENG-4182, ENG-4190 Notes: This is intentionally conservative in scope (does not change default enforcement behavior). See internal runbook for rollback and emergency disable of zone-locker and operator-lease feature gates. For more details see https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4182 and internal doc at docs/security/tenant-zone-locking.md

release_notes: Add tenant zone-locker middleware (feature-gated) to assert tenant geo; Introduce operator-scoped ephemeral KMS lease for operator orchestrator flows; Add audit-stripper pipeline with configurable redaction profiles to reduce PII in high-volume logs; Helm chart knobs for enabling/disabling features; No default behavioral change unless feature gates are turned on.
risk_assessment: Risk: misconfiguration could block legitimate cross-region operator tasks or over-redact audit data. Mitigations: defaults are non-enforcing (soft mode), feature gates and kill-switch route in ingress, rollout to 10% then 100% with monitoring, added metrics zone_enforcement_denied_total and operator_lease_failures_total, and a rollback plan documented in the runbook.
